q: The Banach Contraction Mapping Theorem guarantees a unique fixed point when the map f satisfies:
opts: f is continuous on a compact set
d(f(x),f(y)) ≤ k·d(x,y) for some k<1 and all x,y in a complete metric space
f is Lipschitz with constant exactly 1
exp: A contraction map has Lipschitz constant k<1 on a complete metric space. The unique fixed point is the limit of the sequence x, f(x), f(f(x)), … which is Cauchy.
